quick_english: Now the fourth chapter: the Lord said, thus I taught the imperishable yoga to Vivasvat; Vivasvat spoke it to Manu, and Manu declared it to Ikshvaku.

quick_english: Thus royal sages knew this tradition-received yoga, but it was lost in great time, scorcher of foes; and though obtained by teacher lineage, it is now lost; by this the Lord shows the rarity and weight of this knowledge.

quick_english: That same ancient yoga has been taught to you today; you are my devotee and friend, and this highest secret is so; by the word ca a secondary sense is said, so devotion here is primary toward the teacher, not friendship; this is the purport. Arjuna, though knowing the Lord's own form, asks in the world to make it clear.

quick_english: Though unborn and imperishable in self, though lord of beings, presiding over my own nature, I am born by my own maya.
When duty declines and unrighteousness rises, the Lord creates a self-portion and takes a body to sustain the world.
cite_parts: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata

quick_english: For protecting the good, destroying wrongdoers, and establishing duty, I manifest in every age.
Whoever truly knows my divine birth and action leaves the body without rebirth and comes to me.

Hence, abandoning intention regarding desired objects and fruits, actions that are performed enter the fire of knowledge, whose nature is described and to be described, and are burned.

quick_english: A desireless person with controlled mind and self, having abandoned all possessions, does only bodily action; bodily action is that which is useful to the body and of the nature of sense activity, and it is not tinged by mind and intellect.

quick_english: One who is content with what comes by chance, beyond opposites, free from envy, and equal in success and failure is not bound even while acting. Action binds the agent only by taking on the impurity of desire for fruit; the self binds itself. Otherwise, if inert actions themselves bound, freedom in bondage would not be heartfelt.

quick_english: For one freed of attachment, liberated, mind resting in knowing, acting for sacrifice — all action melts away; and 'for sacrifice' is uttered in the singular, the sacrifices being those described hereafter.

tokens.grounds: Abhinava prose: yajñāya + iti + jāta + eka + vacanam — the singular number of the sacrifice-word

quick_english: The verse says sacrifice in its general nature is brahma offered into brahma-fire by brahma; through brahma-action concentration one goes to brahma. For one engaged, offering in brahma leads to re-entry there. The whole world-souled brahma is the oblation offered in supreme knowledge, in quiet fire, for the increase of radiance. For the yogi whose concentration is such brahma-action, brahma alone is to be gone to and known, and no other fruit is obtained. Limited sacrificers receive limited fruit, while knowers of unlimited complete self-sacrifice do not. The verse binds a supreme secret, explained according to intellect and teacher-tradition; some say instruments and action are brahma-qualifications, but that is to be neglected because the secret tradition-sequence remains unbroken.

quick_english: Even if you are the greatest sinner among all sinners, you will cross all sin by the raft of knowledge.
As a blazing fire reduces fuel to ashes, Arjuna, the fire of knowledge reduces all actions to ashes.
Nothing here is as pure as knowledge; the yogin perfected by yoga finds it in the self in time.
The faithful, intent on that, with restrained senses, obtains knowledge; having obtained knowledge, one quickly attains supreme peace.

The ignorant, faithless, doubting self perishes; there is no world, other world, or happiness for the doubting self. Knowledge-fire arises through practice-born certainty, and nothing equals knowledge in purity.
